newsitem.title: USA: Sinatra in hospital for pinched nerve.
newsitem.headline: Sinatra in hospital for pinched nerve.

text.p: Legendary singer Frank Sinatra was admitted to the hospital on Friday suffering from a pinched nerve, his publicist said.
Susan Reynolds said the singer, who will be 81 next month, was in the Cedars-Sinai medical centre in Beverly Hills undergoing tests.
"It's a pinched nerve, that's all there is," she said, declining to elaborate.
"It's important to say he's in good spirits, talking, walking and has a good appetite," she said.
Sinatra would stay in the hospital for one or two days for tests, she said.
The entertainer cancelled a show in November 1986, for one of the few times in his career, to undergo an emergency operation in Palm Springs. The doctors removed a piece of his large intestine.
